paper_id: Shangguan et al. - 2015 - Relative Localization of RFID Tags using Spatial-Temporal Phase Profiling
title: Relative Localization of RFID Tags using Spatial-Temporal Phase Profiling
motivation: Librarians cannot find misplaced books because existing RFID localization yields absolute coordinates with error margins larger than book spacing; baggage handlers need correct ordering, not absolute positions.
problem_framing: Define relative localization as finding spatial ORDER among tags, not absolute coordinates; error margins of 16cm exceed typical inter-tag distances of 1-10cm.
key_insight: Moving reader creates symmetric V-zone in phase profile with minimum at perpendicular point; ordering tags reduces to finding which V-zones reach their bottom first.
method_signature: STPP uses COTS RFID readers, captures phase sequences over time (phase profiles), applies DTW to detect V-zones despite varying reader speed, quadratic fitting for noise, segmentation for efficiency.
evaluation_criteria: Ordering accuracy (fraction of correctly ordered adjacent tag pairs) in real library and airport deployments with 84% and 95% accuracy respectively.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Phase profiles outside V-zone are fragmentary due to channel instability, making whole-profile connection error-prone; accuracy degrades when tag population exceeds 30 in reading zone.
evidence_for_taste: RSSI values fluctuate and their peak RSSI values appear before the reader moves across them
Phase profiles outside the V-zone are fragmentary
It is thus error-prone to connect the whole profile into a big V-zone
G-RSSI achieves similar low ordering accuracy values of below 25%
Accuracy still has room to improve
the line may not be strictly straight in practice
thinking_moves: 通过移动观察者而非标签来产生相位时间序列
利用物理对称性（距离先减后增）作为定位锚点而非计算绝对距离
将V-zone检测问题转化为序列匹配问题，用DTW处理速度变化
通过分割降采样降低DTW复杂度，从O(MN)降至O(MN/w²)
直接比较V-zone斜率而非拟合参数来确定Y轴顺序
承认方法局限：多径导致相位碎片化，连不成完整V-zone
把感知问题重新定义为通信模式识别问题
